fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility or nighttime conditions can identify it without delay.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence so fire and emergency vehicles are not required to reverse back down the full length of the driveway to exit.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to keep a clear path around it for responders working on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation along the rear of the property to allow responders on foot to reach the back of the residence.
• Keep any gate on the perimeter fencing unlocked or install a Knox-compatible lock so responders can access the rear of the property without delay.
• Mark the rear gate or access point with a reflective marker visible from the access drive.
• Trim shrubs and plantings in the landscaped area that directly border the main residence so responders can move around the building without pushing through dense growth.
• Keep the walkway clear of vegetation overgrowth so responders can move between the front and sides of the residence quickly.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees that hang directly over or touch the house.
• Thin the cluster of trees nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the house.
• Clear shrubs and low branches along the driveway so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Trim low-hanging branches along the driveway to keep the travel path open overhead.
• Separate shrubs from nearby trees so fire cannot move easily from ground level into the tree canopy.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from areas where shrubs and trees are growing close together.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure clear of loose leaves, twigs, and accumulated plant debris.
• Thin scattered trees on the sides of the property where vegetation spacing is tight and trees grow close together.
• Cut back shrubs growing along the edges of the structure to create visible open ground around the foundation.
